summary: The compiler mapping and UTF-8 decoder are well scoped, and the Go tests pass; an additional comparison against Node matched all 165,536 tested byte strings. However, the reused Base64 helper differs from Node for non-ASCII encoded input, leaving the explicit Node-compatibility requirement incomplete.

findings.claim: Delegating to DecodeXBase64 does not preserve Node's handling of non-ASCII characters in the encoded string. That helper filters UTF-8 bytes, whereas Node interprets the low byte of each UTF-16 code unit when decoding Base64. Consequently, characters whose low byte is an alphabet character or '=' can change the decoded text or terminate decoding in Node, but are discarded here. The new DecodeBase64 therefore returns different text for these inputs despite the task's explicit Node-compatibility requirement.
findings.repro: Input encoded = "Y\u0151==" (Yő==): abap.DecodeBase64(&abap.Session{}, encoded) returns "", while node -e 'console.log(JSON.stringify(Buffer.from("Y\u0151==", "base64").toString()))' prints "a". Also, input "YQ😀QUJD" returns Go text "a\x04\x14$", whereas Buffer.from("YQ😀QUJD", "base64").toString() returns "a". Both differences were reproduced using go run /tmp/bench-review-b64.go from tools/gogen/go.
